q: The Brouwer Fixed Point Theorem states that every continuous map f: Dⁿ → Dⁿ (n-disk) has a fixed point. The key topological reason is:
opts: Dⁿ is compact and convex; there is no continuous retraction of Dⁿ onto ∂Dⁿ
f must be a bijection on Dⁿ
exp: Brouwer's theorem follows from the fact that Dⁿ has no retraction onto its boundary Sⁿ⁻¹. If f had no fixed point, the map x ↦ direction from f(x) to x extended to ∂Dⁿ would be such a retraction.
